VECTRA / Brand & market strategy

Capital in motion.
Control by design.

A focused identity for the team behind the treasury. Solana-native operations, deliberate approvals, and a clear path from payment plan to settlement.

Solana-firstOperator-focusedNon-custodial
01 /

Choose a focused position.

Proposed market position

The treasury operations workspace for Solana teams.

For finance and operations leads managing recurring USDC outflows, VECTRA aims to bring payment planning, approval coordination and supported Solana payout workflows into one accountable workflow.

Primary audience

Solana-native teams paying contributors, funding operational wallets and paying contributors in USDC.

Brand promise

Plan the payment. See the costs. Keep signing authority with your treasury.

This is a positioning hypothesis, not a claim of category exclusivity. The opportunity is to make a specific recurring job easier to complete: prepare a USDC distribution, collect approvals, and follow the movement of funds. Live product evidence must substantiate the promise.

03 /

Make the identity recognizable.

Primary mark / forest backgroundDownload SVG ↓
↗

A V built from movement

Converging strokes form a directional V. A detached endpoint suggests a destination and gives the symbol an identifiable detail at small sizes. Keep at least half the symbol width clear around the mark.

Forest#082D23
Signal#B7F59A
Mint#E2F1DB
Canvas#F5F8F3
◒

Green, with a job to do

Forest anchors the brand. Signal highlights direction and selection. Mint frames treasury context. Use deep ink for readable text; approval and error states always include a written label.

Typography / Manrope + DM Sans
Treasury,
in motion.

Manrope for confident headlines and financial totals. DM Sans for controls, labels and operational detail. Use tabular figures for financial tables and restrained spacing for a precise, legible interface.

Graphic language / coordinated paths

Use ordered paths, precise junctions and visible endpoints. They suggest coordination and intent. Treat these as brand graphics, never as a depiction of a verified route or transaction.

04 /

Sound like an operator.

Clear. Calm. Accountable.

Lead with the action and its consequence. Name the asset, approval state and next step. Explain errors in plain language. Distinguish a planned payment, an approved proposal and a settled transaction.

Action“Create payment proposal”
Approval“Awaiting 2 authorized signatures”
Route review“Review fees and destination amount”
Demo state“Illustrative data. No funds moved.”

A consistent message hierarchy

Brand lineTreasury, in motion.
Product descriptorTreasury operations for Solana teams.
TaglineTreasury operations at the speed of Solana.
WorkflowPlan. Approve. Move.
Control promiseCapital in motion. Control by design.

Keep speed as an aspiration. Use measured settlement times, supported routes and real transaction signatures as evidence when available.

05 /

Earn the position through product.

NOW / ESTABLISH

Own the recurring job.

Show the full contributor-payment journey. Use the same V mark, green palette and operational language across the dashboard, onboarding and demo materials.

Validate whether target users can explain VECTRA’s purpose and locate their next action after a brief walkthrough.
NEXT / VALIDATE

Learn from treasury teams.

Run workflow interviews with Solana finance and operations leads. Observe their current approval coordination, recipient management and payment reporting.

Measure setup time, proposal completion, user errors and the manual steps VECTRA could remove. Establish a baseline first.
PROVE / LAUNCH

Replace claims with receipts.

Complete a signed Devnet distribution and a verified supported routing workflow. Publish a walkthrough with actual costs, statuses and transaction evidence.

Report approval-to-settlement time, route outcomes and successful repeat use. Build case studies from observed results, with permission.
Current product boundary: Vectra Lite can connect a wallet and send devnet USDC after simulation. Devnet tokens have no cash value. Mainnet is locked. Illustrative balances, local schedules, and simulated route previews are still labeled as such. Squads approvals and MultiHopper execution remain unconnected. This visual direction is not trademark or name-availability clearance.
